title: First New Orleans Jazz Club meetings and why they disappointed him
summary: Steinau recalls an organizational meeting on Jefferson Davis Parkway, meeting Johnny Wiggs, and later St. Charles Hotel meetings whose music left him unsatisfied.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You know, I don't remember. Let's see. Well, there were, the first one I went to was in a place, I don't recall, was in some, some nightclub, I believe, but I don't have any recollection of what, where it had been.
I don't know what we were talking about.
We were talking about the first Jazz Club meetings that I went to.
Oh yeah, held in some sort of nightclub or something.
Uh, you know, no, I remember what it was. Are you on again? Yeah. Okay. It was in some kind of recreational building on Jefferson Davis Parkway that the
city owned at the time. That comes back to me now. I totally forgot.

And I don't remember anything about it beyond that, except it was a kind of an organizational meeting, much like dozens of other organizational meetings I've been to since. But apparently it took that time, and I remember Myra Menville, Johnny Wiggs, that's where I first met Johnny. Freddie King. Those are about the only people I remember offhand. I remember meetings in the St. Charles Hotel on Sunday afternoons later on, at which there was some music, which was usually not all that great as far as I was concerned. I didn't understand a lot of what was going on, so it wasn't, it didn't seem quite right, but I never quite knew what it was that wasn't quite right about it. And I think maybe in a way that retarded rather than augmented my interest in jazz.
Because I wasn't hearing what I wanted to hear, even though I wasn't quite sure what it was that I wanted to hear, for whatever sense that may make.
